surfaces.part: ground field (full 96x80 tile area, flat earth texture with grass tufts)

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain ground field, not a standing object. The silhouette is a uniform 96-wide block across all 80 rows. The column scans show only mottled earth tones with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical face. Grass tufts and grit are scattered flat details. It has no object front face and no raised volume, so it is a flat texture. Under the terrain kind it reads as 'other' rather than as a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch of the same kind as the grass and paving references. The earth mottling uses about 4-5 brown steps (light dry, mid, dark damp, deep crack lines), plus 2-3 yellow tones in the dry tufts. That matches the grass reference's depth. Measured facts support this: 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference, 2% near-flat coverage against 0%, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The dark crack and clod shading is brown-tinted, not black, so there are no sticker outlines. Texture is spread across tile borders with grit and clods, with no large flat areas. It is slightly less varied than the references, since only 12 colours are used in total and the tufts are sparse. A careful artist would still accept it next to the grass tile.
